title: Venus of Willendorf
summary: The Venus of Willendorf is an 11 cm limestone statuette of a faceless female figure, found on 7 August 1908 at Willendorf II on the Danube in Lower Austria during Josef Szombathy's dig. It dates to roughly 30,000 years ago, in a Gravettian horizon. Its oolitic limestone does not occur near Willendorf and matches rock near Lake Garda in northern Italy. It is held in the Natural History Museum Vienna.

uncertainty.note: Layer 8a is dated younger than 30.8 ka and layer 9 to 29.1–28.8 ka cal BP; the figurine lay about 25 cm below layer 9.

where.modern_name: Willendorf II, near Aggsbach, Lower Austria
where.historical_name: Danube valley loess steppe, Gravettian Europe (no polity)

importance.justification: One of the best-known works of Upper Palaeolithic art, and evidence of long-distance movement of material.
